Commentary.Commentary: The Pakistan bowling was not up to the mark as they were stubbornly unable to take wickets or slow the flow of runs. With quite a few overs left in the day, stay tuned as Pakistan looks to answer the hosts in kind.

That ends a dominating innings for England. With 589 runs on the board, Pakistan sure faces a tough task ahead. Root was undoubtably the highlight of the show, as he picked up where he left off yesterday and was suitably partnered by Woakes.

A brilliant performance by Root on Day 1 gave the English innings a burst of vitality and Cook's ton was the push that the hosts needed.  Pakistan's side did not show the same spark in their bowling and failed to capitalize on their chances. The first session will prove critical for both sides. Pakistan had several chances throughout the day, particularly with captain Cook, but they were let down by some poor fielding which must have been frustrating for Mohammad Amir in particular. Yasir Shah has failed to impress so far, his short deliveries and expensive bowling a far cry from the wicket machine he was in the 1st Test. The rest of the bowlers put in decent efforts but Rahat Ali and Amir were the only ones to pick up wickets with a brace apiece.

As the day progressed, the duo looked relaxed and picked up the run rate. The removal of Cook brought on a brief period of flux but Gary Ballance brought balance back to the game, putting up a 73-run partnership with Root who remained at the crease and has so far scored 141 runs.

What a day it's been for the hosts! England have undoubtedly seized the day and it is all thanks to the deadly duo of Alastair Cook and Joe Root. We take a trip to Old Trafford for the 2nd Test game of the 4-match series between England and Pakistan. The visitors have been in impeccable form in the first Test, handing the English a drubbing and have adapted well to the conditions. This time around too, they will aim to keep up the pressure, with their fearsome bowling attack and their middle order.
